breaking_changes: The version scheme changed from M.m.p to YYYY.WW.N format; CMake version extraction moved to a Python-based git state derivation system, MSI installer versions are reformatted as YY.MM.PATCH, and the get-version action now outputs YYYY.WW.N instead of the static CMake VERSION.

evidence.blockers: No P0 blockers. Five P1 verifications remain: the new /v1/docs API surface, the candidate publishing pipeline, downstream version format handling, the FLM download path, and GGUF architecture compatibility filter policy.
evidence.breaking_changes: The version scheme changed from M.m.p to YYYY.WW.N with corresponding changes to CMake extraction (Python-based), MSI installer version reformat (YY.MM.PATCH), and get-version action output. This is a significant but intentional breaking change documented in RFC #3522, and downstream consumers are listed in the verification to-dos.
evidence.coverage: Reviewed all 38 commits from v11.9.0 to fb6c133c034b7312588ba117e70a61dfd9d32c6b on the main branch. 32 commits were Clean; 6 had notes requiring verification but no blockers.
evidence.manual_testing: New user-facing surfaces require hands-on verification: /v1/docs API with MCP tool integration, the full candidate release pipeline (new shipping surface), FLM ModelScope download paths, and the GGUF compatibility filter's common-denominator policy. Downstream packaging consumers need the YYYY.WW.N version format verified.
evidence.security: No security regressions observed. Security-positive changes include: wildcard origin support with strict scheme enforcement (#3470), removal of the internal MCP client attack surface (#3498), and the GGUF architecture compatibility filter preventing incompatible model downloads (#3198). The FLM ModelScope support (#2841) adds a documented, user-configurable download source.

prioritized_todos.text: Manually test the new /v1/docs index endpoint and individual page fetch in a release candidate build, and verify the lemonade_docs MCP tool works with a standard MCP client (#3347, @anditherobot).

Verify all downstream consumers (Fedora, Debian, MSI, snap, containers) correctly handle the new YYYY.WW.N version format, especially the YY.MM.PATCH reformat for the Windows installer version fields (#3529, @superm1).

Verify the full candidate pipeline end-to-end: push a release-v* branch and confirm candidate-v* tags are created, artifacts publish correctly, MSI signing is skipped, release notes display the unsigned-installer warning, and the generate-release-notes action inputs design is intentional (#3579, @jeremyfowers; #3580, @jeremyfowers; #3581, @jeremyfowers).

Test the FLM download path with default_model_source set to modelscope to confirm --modelscope 1 reaches the flm binary in both load-time and explicit pull paths, and verify JSON API responses for registry_source correctly reflect empty values instead of the default 'huggingface' (#2841, @wariobot09).

Confirm that the GGUF architecture compatibility filter's common-denominator allowlist is an intentional policy and that false negatives for models only supported by newer backend pins (bailingmoe3, kimi-k3) are acceptable, and monitor HF API latency given the extra metadata request now scopes to all HuggingFace operations (#3198, @popey).

tester_plan.changed: The MSI installer version format changed to YY.MM.PATCH to handle the new year.week numbering, and release candidates will produce unsigned MSIs with a SmartScreen warning.

verdict_reason: Five manual verifications before shipping: the new /v1/docs API and MCP tool, the candidate publishing pipeline, downstream compatibility with the new version scheme, the FLM download path, and the GGUF architecture filter — none are P0 blockers, but none can be skipped.
